brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.requirement: One drawer is in the build.
requirements.evidence: No family-drawer part could be placed. The drawer offers need a half base's cut face, and none was offered in any layout I tried (half-e alone, and half-w beside half-e). The only drawer-type piece placed is a bay drawer frame (family bay, 'hex-drawer-frame-bay-s') at cell (0,-1), which is a different family and is not the drawer the brief asks for.

requirements.requirement: One spike is in the build, at the same corner of the same cell as the drawer, touching it.
requirements.evidence: A spike (spike:0#0,0|1,-1|1,0) is placed at the junction of cells (0,0), (1,-1), (1,0). Because no drawer was placed, there is no drawer to share its corner. The bay frame sits in cell (0,-1), which is not one of the spike's three cells, so the spike and the bay do not share a cell corner.

finish.summary: I could not build the requested drawer and spike at the same corner of the same cell. Drawers are only offered at the cut face of a half base, and no layout I tried offered one. The build holds four hex bases (full at (-1,0), (0,0), (1,0), (1,-1)), a bay drawer frame at (0,-1) (a different family from a drawer), and a spike at the junction of (0,0), (1,-1) and (1,0). The configurator check is clear of mesh clashes, with one loose-body warning on the base at (1,0) that joint bolts would lock. Both requirements are unmet.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
